text:
alex: proposing a new canary ramp pattern for model upgrades — trying to avoid flip-flop rollbacks when a brief telemetry blip trips the guards. idea: combine a short hysteresis window with a small "ghost" cohort that follows the primary cohorts but doesn't count toward control decisions unless it stabilizes. thoughts?

 tldr: add a "stability hysteresis" + ghost cohort + explicit rollback grace to the step schedule. keep API ergonomic for customers.

 tess: can you paste a tiny example config? want to see how this looks in the console/API. :eyes:

 alex: sure — rough draft showing both explicit steps and a preset mode: 

 ```json
 {
   "strategy": "ghost_hysteresis",
   "preset": null,
   "steps": [
     {"duration": "10m", "target_pct": 2, "hysteresis_secs": 120},
     {"duration": "20m", "target_pct": 10, "hysteresis_secs": 300},
     {"duration": "30m", "target_pct": 30, "hysteresis_secs": 600},
     {"duration": "60m", "target_pct": 100, "hysteresis_secs": 900, "rollback_grace_secs": 900}
   ],
   "ghost_cohort": {"enabled": true, "offset_pct": 0.5, "stabilize_after_secs": 1800},
   "slo_guards": {"latency_p90_ms": 1200, "error_rate_pct": 0.5},
   "max_surges": 1
 }
 ```

 notes: ghost_cohort.offset_pct = fraction of the current primary cohort that receives requests but is logically insulated until stabilize_after_secs. only once ghost shows stable metrics does it contribute to increasing the primary cohort. hysteresis_secs prevents immediate step advancement/rollback until the metric remains beyond threshold for that duration.

 nish: interesting. couple concerns: 1) telemetry lag — if metrics are delayed we might never meet hysteresis and get stuck, 2) complexity for customers when rounding tiny pct numbers (0.5% ghost on 100k qps?). we should default sane minima and expose a simulation mode in Console.

 priya: agree with simulation. from Console UX POV: expose a "preview simulation" button that runs a short synthetic check and shows estimated time-to-next-step given current metrics + hysteresis. also add toggles: "auto-advance" vs "manual-confirm" and a visible "rollback grace" timer. defaults: min_cohort_size = 1000 requests, stability_window = 5m.

 sanjay: :+1: on rollback_grace. also add a "safety floor" — if target_pct jumps > X% between steps, require a manual confirm. small nit: ghost offset_pct should probably be an absolute safe_min_pct in API to avoid fractional rounding on low-traffic customers.

 deploy-bot: scheduled canary-sim job queued for model v2 -> v3, id=canary-sim-20240405-83. result ETA ~2m.

 alex: good feedback. action items: 1) spike a simulation runner that respects hysteresis/have ghost cohort semantics (nish + priya), 2) API shape PR proposing both "preset" strings (floating_plateau, steady_steps) and explicit "steps" array (alex), 3) Console mockups for preview/sim (priya). i'll add rollback_grace and safety_floor defaults to the draft. tagging @tess for API docs help.

 tess: will draft docs once the PR lands. :thumbsup:

 nish: one more: telemetry team — can we ensure metric windows are aligned to step durations (e.g., p90 computed on the last hysteresis_secs + 30s) so we don't fight sampling windows? i'll ping them.

 alex: yep ping them. will capture in the RFC. thanks all.
